# mibz2

> A bzip2 decoder built for memory-level parallelism.

mibz2 is a bzip2 decoder, block-parallel, its inverse BWT walked as interleaved chains
within each block, with byte-for-byte libbzip2 output and every block and stream CRC
checked, from Python (`mibz2.decompress`, `mibz2.open`) or Rust (`mibz2::decode`,
`mibz2::BzReader`). Install with `pip install mibz2` or `cargo add mibz2`. Each link below
is the Markdown version of a page of https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/.

# Benchmarks

# Benchmarks

mibz2's speed is measured on GitHub's runners by the Benchmark workflow (`.github/workflows/bench.yml`), with the A/B harness `examples/ab.rs` and `bench/report.py`. Nothing about performance is decided on a developer's machine.

- [History](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/benchmarks/history/index.md>): master's figures over its commits.
- [Alternatives](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/benchmarks/alternatives/index.md>): the latest master commit against pbz2 and lbzip2.

These are decoder-level results: one process decoding one file, nothing else. End-to-end results, the decoder inside a pipeline, are in [wikidata-pq's benchmark history](<https://lmmx.github.io/wikidata-pq/guide/bench-history/>).

## What runs when

| event | arms | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a pull request that touches the decoder, the harness, the corpora or the bench | its head and its base (the merge base with master), both built on the runner | one comment on the pull request, edited in place on every push |
| a push to master | mibz2, pbz2 0.2.0 and lbzip2 | the commit's result on the `bench-results` branch, and these pages |
| the Actions tab | either | the run's summary, not recorded |

Only master's commits are recorded. A pull request's runs, and experiments that did not land, are not recorded or shown here; experiments are written up in the [journals](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/background/journals/index.md>).

## The workload

- **The crate's corpora** (`ab gen`, `tests/common/mod.rs`), at scale 4, each compressed by libbzip2 1.0.8 at level 9: `text` (the crate's own sources and README, repeated: 12 MB), `random` (8 MB), `onebyte` (one byte repeated, 20 MB), `pattern` (a 7-byte pattern, 19.6 MB), `runs` (runs of random lengths, 10 MB) and `records` (binary records, 9.6 MB). The `text` corpus is made from the commit's own sources, so its bytes change a little from commit to commit.
- **The Wikidata dump's own blocks:** 12 byte-range windows of 1 MiB of `wikidata-20261019-all.json.bz2`, at (2i + 1)/24 of the file. `examples/windows.rs` keeps each window's whole blocks, their bits untouched, as a stream of its own, checked against libbzip2 and lbzip2: 431 blocks, 11.85 MB of bz2 → 209.7 MB of JSON (17.69×). `bench/wikidata.json` pins each window's offset, length and SHA-256, and the corpus's. Wikimedia serves a dated dump for about six weeks, so the windows are kept on the repository's `bench-data` branch.

## How it is measured

- **A run** is one process decoding one file from disk, end to end, its output hashed (the same hash for every arm, or the run fails: the same-bytes check). It records the wall time, the CPU time (user + sys), the peak RSS, and each thread's CPU.
- **A round** decodes every corpus once with each arm at each thread count: 1 thread (pinned to one CPU) and the runner's cores. The arms' order is rotated and reversed round to round. There are 10 rounds.
- **On a pull request**, the base's own harness binary is an arm (`mibz2@base/ab`), so both builds run in the same process shape on the same runner.
- **Paired ratios:** each round's ratio of one arm's time to the reference arm's (the base; or mibz2, against pbz2 and lbzip2), their geometric mean, and its 95% t-interval over the rounds. A change is called faster or slower only where the interval excludes no change.
- **The bench version** (`bench/report.py`, semver) is stamped on every result. A change to what is measured or how is a new major version, and the history never joins a series across major versions, runner CPU models or sets of corpora.

## The full-dump figure is modelled

Each result also gives a whole dump's decode (103.5 GB of bz2), **modelled, not measured**, from the Wikidata blocks' runs, round by round:

- the scanner's time (the one serial thread: each block's header and Huffman symbols) per byte of bz2, scaled by the dump's bz2 bytes;
- the workers' time per byte of output, scaled by the dump's output, taken as its bz2 bytes times the sample's ratio (17.69×; another sample of the same dump, 24 windows of 25 MB, measured 18.68×; wikidata-pq's CI slice, lines recompressed, is 13.69×);
- at N threads, the larger of the scanner's time and the workers' over N, times the sample's own wall over that bound; the same gap read as a fixed cost is given beside it.

It assumes time linear in bytes, the sample's mix standing for the dump's, and the runner's CPU; its interval carries the rounds' spread and the sample ratio's.

# Alternatives

Loading the chart…

mibz2 beside other bzip2 decoders, pbz2 (Soof Golan's Rust decoder, the harness's dev-dependency) and lbzip2 (C, `lbzip2 -dc -n T`), on master's latest recorded commit, decoded in the same rounds on one runner ([methodology](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/benchmarks/index.md>)). A ratio above 1× is the alternative taking longer (or more memory) than mibz2: there, mibz2 is faster. These are decoder-level results; end-to-end pipeline results are in [wikidata-pq's tracker](<https://lmmx.github.io/wikidata-pq/guide/bench-history/>).

The latest record: [`68e5942`](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/commit/68e594248560bee658a1dbfcf22bcc7bb5c2bde0>) (2026-10-27).

## Where mibz2's CPU goes: the Wikidata blocks at 4 threads (median CPU seconds)

| build | scanner (serial) | workers (summed) | the reading thread and the rest | wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mibz2 | 0.11 | 1.01 | 0.01 | 0.378 |

## Modelled, not measured: a whole dump

The decode of `wikidata-20261019-all.json.bz2` (103 GB of bz2; 1.83 TB of JSON at the sample's 17.69×), scaled from the Wikidata blocks' runs above, round by round (mean ± its 95% interval, the sample ratio's own uncertainty added in):

|  | mibz2 |
| --- | ---: |
| 1 thread | 1h47m ± 13m24s |
| 4 threads | 55m55s ± 8m11s |
| 4 threads, the sample's overlap gap as a fixed cost | 37m26s ± 5m48s |
| the scanner alone (its serial part) | 15m43s ± 26.3s |
| the workers alone, over 4 | 37m26s ± 5m48s |

At 4 threads the workers bound it. Per byte: the scanner 9.1 ns a byte of bz2, the workers 4.91 ns a byte of output at 4 threads (CPU, summed over them), 3.00 ns at 1 thread (wall, less the scanner's part); the scanner would bind from about 10 worker threads (mibz2).

**What the model assumes**

\- \*\*Linear in bytes:\*\* the scanner's time in the dump's bz2 bytes, the workers' in its output bytes. - \*\*The sample stands for the dump:\*\* 12 windows of 1 MiB at (2i + 1)/24 of the dump, 431 of its own blocks; their mix of entities and their ratio, 17.69× (the windows' 95% interval ±14.0%), stand for the whole dump's. Another sample of the same dump (wikidata-pq's bench/full, 24 windows of 25 MB) measured 18.68×; wikidata-pq's CI slice, lines recompressed, is 13.69×. - \*\*The wall at N threads\*\* is the larger of the scanner's time and the workers' time over N (the scanner is one thread; the workers run blocks in parallel), times the sample's own wall over that bound: its overlap and fill taken to grow with the work, which errs long. Read as a fixed cost instead, the same gap gives the third row. - \*\*The machine is this runner,\*\* reading the dump from page cache: no download, no disk, no other work. The output is hashed by the reading thread and discarded. - The uncertainty is the rounds' spread, with the sample ratio's added in quadrature to the part that scales with the output; not the runner's: another CPU model gives other figures.

**The corpora, the machine and the toolchain**

| corpus | bz2 bytes | output bytes | SHA-256 | source | |---|--:|--:|---|---| | \`wikidata\` | 11,854,933 | 209,700,196 | \`82f65ace0731962d…\` | wikidata-20261019-all.json.bz2: 12 windows' whole blocks (bench/wikidata.json) | | \`onebyte\` | 51 | 20,000,000 | \`22924f5b3187645f…\` | ab gen (tests/common/mod.rs corpora), libbzip2 -9 | | \`pattern\` | 1,116 | 19,600,000 | \`0f07e2a274b91896…\` | ab gen (tests/common/mod.rs corpora), libbzip2 -9 | | \`random\` | 7,097,921 | 8,000,000 | \`10d444e6204289af…\` | ab gen (tests/common/mod.rs corpora), libbzip2 -9 | | \`records\` | 9,587,840 | 9,600,000 | \`ff8b5f6ed3dd4445…\` | ab gen (tests/common/mod.rs corpora), libbzip2 -9 | | \`runs\` | 37,995 | 10,000,235 | \`af3be4d130faf312…\` | ab gen (tests/common/mod.rs corpora), libbzip2 -9 | | \`text\` | 855,578 | 12,074,837 | \`c5bc082b847602ba…\` | ab gen (tests/common/mod.rs corpora), libbzip2 -9 | - CPU: AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor, 4 cores, reported clock 4370.5 MHz (cycles a byte use it), flags avx2, avx512f, bmi1, bmi2, pclmulqdq, sse4\_1, ssse3; kernel 7.0.0-1017-azure; image ubuntu24 20261026.354.1 - rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13); pbz2 0.2.0 (a dev-dependency, the harness's arm); lbzip2 version 2.5 - bench 1.0.0 (bench/report.py), 10 rounds, threads 1, 4

# Concepts

# Concepts

mibz2 decodes bzip2 as libbzip2 1.0.8 defines it, byte for byte, with every check libbzip2 makes, and decodes several blocks at once.

- [What is checked, and when](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/concepts/checks/index.md>): block CRCs, stream CRCs, what an error reports, and the four inputs mibz2 refuses where libbzip2 does not.
- [How it works](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/concepts/how-it-works/index.md>): the one sequential phase (the scanner), the workers, and the inverse BWT walked as 12 interleaved chains.
- [Prior work](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/concepts/prior-work/index.md>): libbzip2; Kärkkäinen, Kempa and Puglisi (DCC 2012); lbzip2 and pbzip2.

# What is checked, and when

## Block CRCs, before the block's bytes

Every block's CRC is checked before any of that block's bytes are returned. A block whose CRC does not match returns none of its bytes: the error comes instead. The bytes returned before an error are exactly the stream's up to the bad block.

## Stream CRCs, at the stream's end

Each stream's combined CRC is checked at the stream's end. The bytes of a stream's blocks are returned as each block is verified, before the stream's own CRC has been read. So a streaming caller has the whole stream verified only once a read reaches its end without an error: until then, what it has read is provisional.

In Python, `BZ2Reader.verified` turns true only when a read returns the end with every block's and stream's CRC matched.

## Where an error was found

An error says where decoding failed: in Rust `Error { kind, block, bit }`, in Python the `DecodeError` message. That is which block, and the bit it starts at. A damaged bit can be found later than where it lies, since the input is only known to be wrong once something it encodes fails a check.

The error kinds (`ErrorKind`):

- the input: `Empty`, `NotBz2`, `Truncated`, `TrailingData`;
- each of libbzip2's block checks: `BadBlockMagic`, `BadOrigPtr`, `NoSymbols`, `BadGroups`, `BadSelectors`, `BadSelector`, `BadCodeLength`, `BadHuffmanCode`, `SelectorOverrun`, `RunTooLong`, `BlockTooLong`, `RunUnfinished`;
- `BlockCrc` and `StreamCrc`, with the stored and computed values;
- this decoder's refusals: `Randomised`, `BlockTooLarge`;
- `Io` (from a `BzReader`'s source), `RangeOvershoot`, `Cancelled`, and `Internal` (a caught panic: a bug).

## What is decoded, and what is refused

The format is libbzip2 1.0.8's, with every check it makes: bzip2 1.0 and later output. Four choices differ from it, and each has its own error:

| input | libbzip2 | mibz2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| randomised blocks (written only by bzip2 0.9.0 and earlier, before 1999) | decoded | refused (`Randomised`) |
| bytes after the last stream that do not begin another stream | ignored | an error (`TrailingData`): nothing after a stream is silently dropped |
| an oversubscribed Huffman code pointing past the alphabet | a stale table entry read | an error |
| a block whose compressed form passes 64 MiB (a real block is at most about 4.2 MB) | decoded | an error (`BlockTooLarge`) |

# How it works

## Threads

- **The scanner.** One thread reads each block's header and Huffman-coded symbols in order. This is the one sequential phase: a block's end is known only once its symbols are read. It finds blocks exactly, not by searching for the block magic, so a magic inside a block's data is never taken for a block. It is roughly a tenth of a decode on well-compressed text, more on poorly compressible data.
- **The workers.** Each worker finishes a block: move-to-front, the T-vector, the inverse BWT walk, RLE1 and the CRC.
- **The reader** takes the blocks in order. A block's error reaches the reader only once every block before it has been read.
- **Memory is bounded:** at most `slots` blocks are in flight (by default twice the threads), and the buffers are reused from block to block.

With one thread, the same phases run in order on the calling thread.

## The walk

The inverse BWT is a chain of dependent loads: each step's row is the previous step's load. A plain walk keeps one load in flight. The default walk (`bwt::walk_segments`) keeps a dozen:

- 256 pseudo-random rows, the walk's first among them, are segment starts;
- a bitmap of the starts ends each segment;
- 12 lanes walk segments in lockstep, each taking the next segment when its own ends;
- the segments are joined in order.

It equals the plain walk on every list, lists of several cycles included: the join follows the segments' links until the block's length is reached. Blocks under 64 Ki are walked plainly. The kernel is behind `bwt::InverseBwt` (`Segmented`, the default; `Plain`), so a walk can be swapped and timed as part of the whole decoder.

## Kernels

`Kernels::detect()` chooses at run time: AVX2 (with BMI1) for move-to-front and RLE1, and PCLMULQDQ for the CRC. Each has a scalar twin, used on any other CPU and on aarch64 (`Kernels::scalar()`). The walk's gain is scalar code, memory-level parallelism, so it holds on any CPU.

# Prior work

- **The format and its checks are libbzip2's** (Julian Seward, bzip2 1.0.8, `decompress.c`). mibz2 follows its decoding rules and makes each of its checks, in its terms. Its Huffman decode tables are built as `BZ2_hbCreateDecodeTables` builds them, so a stream libbzip2 refuses is refused here too. It is a separate implementation in Rust, not a port of libbzip2's code. The tests use libbzip2 itself (the `bzip2` crate's bundled 1.0.8) as the oracle.
- **Interleaving several traversals of one BWT inversion** on one thread, so that out-of-order execution keeps their loads in flight, is Kärkkäinen, Kempa and Puglisi's idea: "Slashing the Time for BWT Inversion", DCC 2012, pp. 99–108.

  - They also use a super-alphabet (an LF² table: two characters a dependent lookup) and "Precopy" for repetitive data. Neither is used here.
  - What is particular here is only how the traversals are found in an existing bzip2 file, which carries no metadata for them: the random starts, the stop bitmap, and the joining in order.
- **Block-parallel decoding** is lbzip2's (Mikołaj Izdebski) and pbzip2's approach.
- **pbz2** (Soof Golan) arrived independently at a segmented, multi-chain walk too; the bake-off that found it is in the [journals](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/background/journals/index.md>).

# Get started

# Installation

## Python

mibz2 needs Python 3.10 or later. It has no Python dependencies.

```sh
pip install mibz2
```

or with uv:

```sh
uv add mibz2
```

Wheels are built for Linux (x86-64, aarch64), macOS (x86-64, arm64) and Windows (x64). Each uses the stable ABI (abi3), so one wheel covers every Python version from 3.10.

## Rust

```sh
cargo add mibz2
```

The library depends on std only. Its minimum supported Rust version is 1.80. The `python` feature builds the Python extension module, and is only for maturin.

# Quickstart

## Python

Write a .bz2 file with the standard library's `bz2`, to have one to read:

```python
import bz2

with bz2.open("sample.bz2", "wb") as f:
    for i in range(10_000):
        f.write(f"line {i}\n".encode())
```

A whole file in memory, decoded on every CPU this process may use, or on one thread:

```pycon
>>> import mibz2
>>> compressed = open("sample.bz2", "rb").read()
>>> data = mibz2.decompress(compressed)
>>> data == bz2.decompress(compressed)
True
>>> mibz2.decompress(compressed, threads=1) == data
True
```

A file read as it is decoded: `open` takes a path or a binary file object, and returns a buffered binary file. Its `raw.verified` turns true once a read has reached the end with every block's and stream's CRC matched:

```pycon
>>> with mibz2.open("sample.bz2") as f:
...     first = f.readline()
...     before = f.raw.verified
...     rest = f.read()
...     after = f.raw.verified
>>> first, before, after
(b'line 0\n', False, True)
```

A bad input raises `mibz2.DecodeError`, a `ValueError`, from `decompress` or from the read at which it is found. The message says which block and bit decoding failed at:

```pycon
>>> damaged = bytearray(compressed)
>>> damaged[len(damaged) // 2] ^= 0x10
>>> try:
...     mibz2.decompress(bytes(damaged))
... except mibz2.DecodeError as e:
...     print(type(e).__name__, isinstance(e, ValueError))
DecodeError True
```

## Rust

```rust
use std::io::Read;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // a whole .bz2 in memory (its streams one after another): on this thread, or on 4
    let data = std::fs::read("file.bz2")?;
    let text = mibz2::decode(&data)?;
    let same = mibz2::decode_parallel(&data, 4)?;
    assert_eq!(text, same);

    // any Read, as a Read: on this thread, or block-parallel on 4 worker threads
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    mibz2::BzReader::parallel(std::fs::File::open("file.bz2")?, 4).read_to_end(&mut out)?;
    Ok(())
}
```

A bad stream is an `mibz2::Error` (its `kind`, `block` and `bit`), or from a `BzReader` an `io::Error` of kind `InvalidData` wrapping it. The [Rust reference](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/reference/rust/index.md>) lists the rest: the push decoder, the block scanner and the decoding of a range of blocks.

# Optional

# History

- **In wikidata-pq.** mibz2 was written in [lmmx/wikidata-pq](<https://github.com/lmmx/wikidata-pq>), whose split decodes the Wikidata JSON dump. A profile there found the bz2 decode about half of the split's CPU, bound by the inverse BWT's chain of dependent loads, and a prototype walked it as interleaved chains (lmmx/wikidata-pq\#194). The production decoder followed behind a flag (`WIKIDATA_BZ2_DECODER=native`, lmmx/wikidata-pq\#197): on CI, the split's CPU fell 20.6% and its wall 16.6% against lbzip2.
- **The bake-off.** Before going further, it was timed against pbz2, fbz, the `lbzip2` crate, indexed\_bzip2, lbzip2 and libbzip2 on the dump's blocks. pbz2 0.2.0 tied it; the others were 1.5–1.9× slower at 4 threads (lmmx/wikidata-pq\#199).
- **Its own repository.** The decoder's history moved to [lmmx/mibz2](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2>) by `git filter-repo`, its paths renamed and each `#N` in its commit messages rewritten to `lmmx/wikidata-pq#N`, with its journals. It was published as 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 on crates.io and PyPI, the crate and the Python package at one version.

The [journals](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/background/journals/index.md>) record each step.

# Journals

mibz2's development is recorded in dated entries in [docs/journal/](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/tree/master/docs/journal>), written to the format in [docs/JOURNAL.md](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/JOURNAL.md>). Experiments that did not land are recorded there, not in the benchmark's history.

| entry | what it records |
| --- | --- |
| [compute frontier](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/journal/2026-10-27-compute-frontier.md>) | where wikidata-pq's split spent its CPU, and the prototype kernels: the interleaved walk first measured |
| [BWT inversion literature](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/journal/2026-10-27-bwt-inversion-literature.md>) | an inventory of the literature on inverting the BWT |
| [bz2 decoder](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/journal/2026-10-27-bz2-decoder.md>) | the production decoder: its design, its correctness evidence (libbzip2, real dump blocks, fuzzing) and CI's figures |
| [bz2 bake-off](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/journal/2026-10-27-bz2-bakeoff.md>) | mibz2 against pbz2, fbz, the `lbzip2` crate, indexed\_bzip2, lbzip2 and libbzip2 |
| [mibz2 v2](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/journal/2026-10-27-mibz2-v2.md>) | the second round's plan, and the A/B harness (`examples/ab.rs`) |
| [mibz2 repository](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/journal/2026-10-27-mibz2-repository.md>) | the move to this repository, the Python package and the release workflows |
| [site and bench tracker](<https://github.com/lmmx/mibz2/blob/master/docs/journal/2026-10-27-site-and-bench-tracker.md>) | this site, the CI benchmark and its tracker |

# Development

## Layout

| path | contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/` | the crate: the bit reader, block parsing, MTF, the inverse BWT, RLE1, the CRC, streams, the parallel decoder, `BzReader`, and `python.rs` (the extension module, feature `python`) |
| `tests/` | the Rust tests against libbzip2 (`decode.rs`, `corpus.rs`), their corpora in `tests/common/` |
| `examples/` | `ab` (the A/B harness), `bzcat`, `fuzz` (a mutation fuzz loop), `windows` (real dump windows checked) |
| `benches/` | `cargo bench` |
| `bench/` | the CI benchmark's scripts and its pinned Wikidata windows |
| `python/mibz2/` | the Python package, and `_mibz2.pyi`, the stub of the compiled module |
| `python/tests/` | the Python tests |
| `docs/site/` | this site; `docs/journal/` the development journals |

## Building and testing

The tools: a Rust toolchain, [uv](<https://docs.astral.sh/uv/>), [just](<https://just.systems/>), and for the lints taplo, whitespace-format and cargo-machete.

```sh
just py         # maturin develop, then pytest
just test-ci    # cargo test and the doc tests
just clippy     # clippy on every target and feature, warnings as errors
just pc         # formatting and lints (as pre-commit runs them)
cargo test --release                                   # against libbzip2
cargo run --release --example fuzz -- 600 1            # a mutation fuzz loop, libbzip2 the oracle
cargo run --release --example bzcat -- 4 < f.bz2 > f   # the parallel decoder as a command
```

On aarch64: `rustup target add aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `apt install qemu-user gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu`, then `cargo test --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu --config .cargo/aarch64-qemu.toml`.

## Benchmarking

Performance is measured on CI (`.github/workflows/bench.yml`, the [benchmark](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/benchmarks/index.md>)): a pull request that touches the decoder gets a comment with its head against its base. Locally, the same harness:

```sh
cargo build --release --example ab
target/release/examples/ab gen corpora 4
target/release/examples/ab run runs.jsonl --arms mibz2,pbz2,lbzip2 --threads 1,4 --rounds 5 corpora/*.bz2
target/release/examples/ab summary runs.jsonl
```

## Commits

Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](<https://www.conventionalcommits.org/>) (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `ci:` ...); the `conventional-pre-commit` hook checks them. `release-plz.toml` groups the changelog by these prefixes.

# Documentation

The site is built with [Zensical](<https://zensical.org/>) from `docs/site/` and `zensical.toml`. The Python API reference is generated by mkdocstrings from the package's docstrings and the compiled module's stub (`python/mibz2/_mibz2.pyi`).

```sh
just docs-serve   # build, serve and rebuild on change
just docs-check   # strict build, site checks, and the pages' examples as tests
```

- `docs/scripts/check_site.py` checks that every page is in the nav, that internal links and anchors resolve, that every page has a description matching its llms.txt entry, and that every public name is in the API reference.
- `docs/conftest.py` runs each page's Python examples with pytest (`pytest docs/site`); a `pycon` block's output must match.
- `docs/scripts/bench_history.py` turns the `bench-results` branch into the benchmark pages' data (`docs/site/assets/bench-history.json`) and tables (`docs/generated/`) before each build. Without a checkout of the branch (`--store`), it reads `origin/bench-results`, or writes empty ones.

## Publishing

`.github/workflows/site.yml` builds the site on every push to master, and after each Benchmark run on master, and publishes it to the `gh-pages` branch, served at [https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/>). A pull request from this repository gets a preview under `pr-preview/pr-<number>/`, linked from a comment on the pull request and removed when it closes. Previews start once the repository's Pages source is set to the `gh-pages` branch.

# Releasing

The crate and the Python package are released at one version, from one commit.

## Deploy Release

Run the **Deploy Release** workflow (`deploy.yml`) with a bump (patch, minor or major). It runs `just release`, which:

1. bumps the version in `pyproject.toml` (`uv version --bump`) and sets the crate's in `Cargo.toml` to match;
2. writes the crate's changelog with release-plz;
3. commits `chore(release): bump 🐍 -> vX.Y.Z` and tags `py-X.Y.Z`;
4. pushes the commit and the tag, then starts **CI** on the tag (a tag pushed with the workflow's token starts no workflow by itself).

CI on a `py-*` tag builds the wheels and the sdist and publishes them to PyPI, and publishes the crate to crates.io with release-plz (which tags `mibz2-vX.Y.Z` and makes the GitHub release). Both use Trusted Publishing, in the `pypi` and `crates-io` environments.

## Out-of-band cases

- **Tag Release** (`tag.yml`): tags an existing commit `py-<version>` at the version its `pyproject.toml` and `Cargo.toml` already hold (no bump), and starts CI on the tag. Each registry is skipped where it already has the version.
- **Release Notes** (`release-notes.yml`): makes a version's GitHub release (`v<version>`) at a given commit if it does not exist, or updates its notes, from that version's section of `CHANGELOG.md`.

# Reference

# Reference

| language | page |
| --- | --- |
| Python | [mibz2](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/reference/api/mibz2/index.md>) |
| Rust | [mibz2](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/reference/rust/index.md>), and its full documentation on [docs.rs](<https://docs.rs/mibz2>) |

# mibz2

mibz2: a fast bzip2 decoder, block-parallel and multi-chain within each block.

- `decompress`: a whole .bz2 in memory, decoded.
- `open`: a .bz2 file (a path or a binary file object) read as a buffered binary file, decoded as it is read.

Every block's CRC is checked before any of that block's bytes are returned, and each stream's combined CRC is checked at the stream's end. Bytes read from a stream before its end come from blocks whose own CRCs matched, but the stream as a whole is verified only when a read reaches its end: until then, treat what has been read as provisional (see `BZ2Reader.verified`).

## DecodeError

Bases: `ValueError`

The input is not valid bzip2 data.

## decompress

```python
decompress(data: bytes | bytearray, threads: int | None = None) -> bytes
```

Decode a whole .bz2 (its streams one after another), every CRC checked.

It runs on every CPU this process may use, or on `threads`.

Raises:

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `DecodeError` | When the input is not valid bzip2 data. |

## BZ2Reader

```python
BZ2Reader(source: Source, threads: int | None = None)
```

Bases: `RawIOBase`

A .bz2 file's decoded bytes, read in order (an unbuffered binary file).

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `Source` | A path, or a binary file object open for reading (its `read` is called). | *required* |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | Decoding threads: `1` decodes on the reading thread; more decode that many blocks at once on worker threads. `None` (the default) uses every CPU this process may use. | `None` |

Raises:

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `DecodeError` | From a read, when the input is not valid bzip2 data: a block whose CRC does not match (none of its bytes are returned), a stream whose combined CRC does not match (raised by the read that reaches the stream's end), or a malformed or truncated stream. The error says which block and bit it was found at, which is where decoding failed and need not be where the input was damaged. |

### readable

```python
readable() -> bool
```

True: a reader is readable.

### readinto

```python
readinto(b) -> int
```

Read up to `len(b)` decoded bytes into `b`; 0 at the end (when verified).

### verified

```python
verified: bool
```

True once a read has reached the end and every block's and stream's CRC matched.

Until then, the bytes read so far have each passed their block's CRC, but the stream's combined CRC has not yet been checked.

### close

```python
close() -> None
```

Stop decoding (its worker threads stop) and close the reader.

## open

```python
open(
    source: Source, threads: int | None = None, buffer_size: int = 1 << 20
) -> BufferedReader[BZ2Reader]
```

Open a .bz2 file for reading, decoded as it is read.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `Source` | A path, or a binary file object open for reading. | *required* |
| `threads` | `int \| None` | Decoding threads, as for `BZ2Reader`. | `None` |
| `buffer_size` | `int` | The buffered reader's buffer, in bytes. | `1 << 20` |

Returns:

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `BufferedReader` | A buffered binary file over a `BZ2Reader` (its `raw`), whose `raw.verified` says whether the whole input has been read and verified. |

Examples:

```pycon
>>> import bz2, mibz2, tempfile, os
>>> path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "a.bz2")
>>> with bz2.open(path, "wb") as f:
...     _ = f.write(b"line one\nline two\n")
>>> with mibz2.open(path) as f:
...     lines = f.readlines()
...     verified = f.raw.verified
>>> lines, verified
([b'line one\n', b'line two\n'], True)
```

# mibz2 (Rust)

The crate's API documentation is on [docs.rs](<https://docs.rs/mibz2>).

| API | what |
| --- | --- |
| `decode`, `decode_parallel(data, threads)` | a whole .bz2 in memory |
| `BzReader::new(r)`, `BzReader::parallel(r, threads)`, `parallel_with(r, threads, slots, kernels)` | a `Read` adaptor; a bad stream is an `io::Error` (`InvalidData`) wrapping `mibz2::Error` |
| `StreamDecoder::new(threads, slots, kernels)` | the push form: `write` compressed chunks from one thread, `read` decoded bytes from another, `close`, `cancel`; at most `slots` blocks in flight |
| `scan(data)` → `BlockSpan { index, start_bit, end_bit, crc, stream, level }` | block boundaries, without decoding |
| `decode_blocks(data, start_bit, end_bit, level, kernels, out)` → `Range` | a range of whole blocks, each CRC checked |
| `Error { kind: ErrorKind, block, bit }` | what is wrong with the input, and where |
| `Kernels::detect()`, `Kernels::scalar()` | the SIMD kernels, or the portable ones |
| `bwt::InverseBwt` (`Segmented`, the default; `Plain`), `decode_with::<I>`, `StreamDecoder::with_inverse::<I>` | the inverse-BWT kernel, swappable and timeable as part of the whole decoder |

```rust
// the block boundaries (each block's header and Huffman symbols read, nothing decoded),
// then any range of whole blocks decoded on its own, on any thread
let data = std::fs::read("file.bz2")?;
for span in mibz2::scan(&data) {
    let span = span?;
    let mut part = Vec::new();
    let range = mibz2::decode_blocks(&data, span.start_bit, span.end_bit, span.level,
                                      mibz2::Kernels::detect(), &mut part)?;
    // range.blocks: each block's (start bit, end bit, CRC); mibz2::combine(...) gives a
    // stream's combined CRC from its blocks'
}
```

# Start here

# mibz2

A bzip2 decoder built for memory-level parallelism.

mibz2 decodes bzip2. It is block-parallel, as lbzip2 is. Within a block, its inverse BWT is walked as 12 interleaved chains, so a core keeps a dozen of the walk's cache-missing loads in flight instead of one.

- Its output is byte for byte libbzip2's, and every block CRC and stream CRC is checked.
- It runs on any x86-64 or aarch64 CPU. Its SIMD kernels (AVX2, PCLMULQDQ) are chosen at run time, and each has a portable scalar twin.
- The library depends on std only.

```pycon
>>> import mibz2
>>> data = mibz2.decompress(open("file.bz2", "rb").read())
>>> data[:18]
b'line one\nline two\n'
>>> with mibz2.open("file.bz2") as f:
...     lines = f.readlines()
...     verified = f.raw.verified
>>> len(lines), verified
(2000, True)
```

Its name is for "multi-chain inversion of bzip2". It was written in [wikidata-pq](<https://github.com/lmmx/wikidata-pq>), to decode the Wikidata dump, and knows nothing of Wikidata ([history](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/background/history/index.md>)).

## Where to go

- [Installation](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/getting-started/installation/index.md>) and the [quickstart](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/getting-started/quickstart/index.md>), in Python and in Rust.
- [What is checked, and when](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/concepts/checks/index.md>): each block's CRC before its bytes are returned, each stream's at its end, and what an error reports.
- [How it works](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/concepts/how-it-works/index.md>): the scanner, the workers and the multi-chain walk.
- [Benchmarks](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/benchmarks/index.md>): master's figures over its commits, and mibz2 against pbz2 and lbzip2.
- [Reference](<https://lmmx.github.io/mibz2/reference/index.md>): the Python API, and the Rust API on docs.rs.

## Install

```sh
pip install mibz2   # Python 3.10+
cargo add mibz2     # Rust
```
